text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The chairman of the Coalition Party and ex-prime minister Tiit Vaehi says the party may split at a congress in December if the government, dominated by the Coalition Party, does not make serious political changes and imposes customs tariffs.
- Finland signed an agreement on 5.4 million kroons support to the Estonian Migration Fund to help Russian officers who want to leave Estonia.
- A small commune in eastern Estonia has agreed to the establishing of a refugee camp on its territory, hoping for more income and new jobs.
- Estonian woman athlete Tiia Eeskivi's four-year ban from competition after a positive drugs test was shortened to two years by the IAAF congress in Athens.
- Retired Russian officers who reside in Estonia cannot be mobilised to active service, said Vyacheslav Kirillov, press spokesman of the Russian Embassy in Tallinn.
- The privatisation agency made a profit of 8.9 billion kroons over four years of activity, the agency said.
- China invited Defence Minister Andrus Oovel for a visit in April-May next year, the defence ministry said.

- Imposing customs tariffs in Estonia is not an urgent matter and should be done according to agreements between Estonia and the European Union, EU Commissioner on agriculture and rural life Franz Fischler said in Tallinn.
